subject: general
question: Which of the following diseases is caused by bacteria?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Anthrax**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anthrax** is a serious infectious disease caused by gram-positive, rod-shaped bacteria known as *Bacillus anthracis*.
 
• It is primarily a disease of herbivorous animals, but humans can become infected through direct or indirect contact with sick animals.
 
• The disease can manifest in three forms: cutaneous (skin), inhalational (lungs), and gastrointestinal (digestive system).
 
• Anthrax is not contagious and cannot be spread directly from person to person.
 
• The bacteria can form spores that can survive in harsh conditions for decades, making it a potential bioterrorism agent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smallpox** is caused by the variola virus, not bacteria.
 
• **Rabies** is caused by the rabies virus, not bacteria.
 
• **AIDS** is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), not bacteria.
 
• Bacterial infections are typically treated with antibiotics, whereas viral infections require antiviral medications or other treatments.
